title: The ready push makes the merge tree equal the head tree, so main's push run skips by the existing rule
why: Source: the consultant's measured read at 12:15 CST Nov 14 (owner goal: CI speed, top priority), one tree pair re-read by the coordinator (coordinator 12:16, relayed; triage read none of it). Facts: REST read at 12:14: the last 8 main push `checks` runs each ran 30 of 33-35 jobs; the push skip fired 0 of 8. Cause as read: the merged tree never equals the green PR head tree (strict=false: the head is behind main at merge). The pair the coordinator read: #3402 head ef8582befd5f tree 2c29427dc8; merge 245e168db806 tree 28705afa96. Cost: a full run on main per merge (the run for 415e8b51b was still going at 31 min); its queued legs held the next ready mark (#3158 unmarked about 40 min). Proposal (the consultant's, no rule change): the ready-time records push becomes a merge of origin/main plus the records commit; if nothing merges during that PR's CI, the head tree equals the merge tree and main's push run skips by the existing rule (owner ruling push-skip-proven-tree, 12:18 CST Nov 13, item 729 a: skip the push re-run when the pushed tree equals the tree the PR tested). Risks the coordinator named in the lane's brief: a one-parent records commit after a record makes it stale (cost #3405 a fix check at 11:36), and overlap with #3396 (step records-page-before-ready, held on owner item 830). The standing grant lets the batch runner push a plain merge of main into a handed-in PR; each new head gets a fix verifier and a fresh review log. Related: owner item 830; steps records-page-before-ready, push-skip-proven-tree, tree-equal-skip-mutation-prs. Also asked: runner 11 reads the last 8 main push runs of home and degen the same way (they use the same push skip). Lane started 12:16 CST by the coordinator (session_013NEJKyzT11AdU32mgrLnAC) with a first deliverable before any build: design, the record-staleness answer, overlap with #3396, and whether an owner pick is needed; it stops there if one is. A guard-or-check change: if a verdict moves, round 3 applies. OWNER ITEM 840 12:20 CST Nov 14 (lane ready-push-merges-main via coordinator 12:18, relayed; triage read none of it): the lane built nothing and waits. Item 840 (pick-ready-push-merge-main) is on the page, linked to item 830. Making `merge <pr> --ready` push a merge of main widens what the merge tool does to a PR branch, and the records commit that `--ready` also pushes is a one-parent commit that makes the review record stale. Lane's code read: `draft_step` in merge/merge.py never pushes a merge today (`holds_base`, rule M3, lets a head lacking main's tip stand if the merge is clean); `live_review_state` ends its walk as stale at any one-parent commit, in either order; the lane-lint walk (about merge.py line 1861) already skips a page-only commit. One full checks run after the records step took 44 min (#3396's body, n=1). Options: a merge main at ready and the record skips page-only commits (widens; the lane recommends it; never starred), b merge main only and the record goes stale when the page changes, c leave it, d answer item 830 first (starred at the coordinator's recommendation, with b as its fallback).
